projects.title: RFID Student Access
projects.tagline: Local-first door access for schools and makerspaces.
projects.summary: A self-hosted badge access system for classrooms, labs, and student workshops—built on inexpensive ESP microcontrollers with zero monthly cloud fees.
projects.whatItSolves: Most commercial door systems lock schools into pricey subscriptions and put the door relay right behind the outside plastic reader where it can be tampered with. We split the reader and the lock controller into two separate boards and run the dashboard right on the local network.
highlights: Two-part hardware: the reader stays outside, the lock switch stays safely inside
Works 100% on your local network—doors still open even if the internet goes down
Simple web dashboard for adding student cards and checking lab attendance

setupSteps.title: Flash the two controller boards
setupSteps.detail: Upload `esp/InputNode.ino` to the exterior reader board and `esp/OutputNode.ino` to the interior relay board.

setupSteps.title: Start the local dashboard
setupSteps.detail: Open `server/frontend/index.html` on any local machine or Raspberry Pi to manage student cards and room access.

projects.title: Macro 3×3 Pad
projects.tagline: A 9-key shortcut pad that remembers your keys on the chip.
projects.summary: A compact 3×3 mechanical keypad that saves your shortcuts directly to onboard memory—so you never need bloated background software running on your PC.
projects.whatItSolves: Big keyboard brands force you to install 500MB apps and sign into cloud accounts just to bind a shortcut key—and the moment you plug into another computer, your bindings disappear. Macro saves your 9 shortcuts right on the microcontroller.
highlights: Set your keys once with a lightweight Python app, then close it forever
Shortcuts live on the hardware chip (EEPROM)—plug into any Linux, Mac, or Windows machine
Acts as a standard USB keyboard out of the box with zero drivers

setupSteps.title: Upload the Arduino sketch
setupSteps.detail: Flash `3x3/simple/usb/simple.ino` onto your microcontroller wired to a 3×3 switch grid.

setupSteps.title: Bind your keys in seconds
setupSteps.detail: Run `macro_pad_config.py`, click any of the 9 buttons, press your shortcut combo, and hit Save to Device.
setupSteps.command: pip install pyserial keyboard && python3 macro_pad_config.py

projects.title: Mateo Weather Network
projects.tagline: Community weather stations for cities, farms, and off-grid valleys.
projects.summary: An open-source, solar-powered weather network that brings accurate local forecasts to places commercial stations ignore—and the visual foundation for Eggman Studios.
projects.whatItSolves: Professional weather stations cost thousands of dollars, while cheap home sensors give false readings whenever the sun hits them. Mateo pairs sub-$100 solar hardware with automatic neighbor cross-checking to filter out bad data.
highlights: Three station setups for city balconies, rural farms, and off-grid villages
Automatic quality checks spot and ignore sensor spikes before they skew the map
Solar-powered design that runs for months without direct sunlight

setupSteps.title: Clone the Mateo & WEB-Projekt repo
setupSteps.detail: Explore the station manual (`templates/stationinfo.html`), web platform (`templates/index.html`), and Tailwind CSS design system.

setupSteps.title: Build or customize the web interface
setupSteps.detail: Recompile the stylesheet whenever you tweak the layout or color tokens.
